Q: How to prevent creation of evdev input node A:

To the best of my understanding, udev doesn't have a way to prevent the node's creation, so you have to:

  1. Use udevadm info -a -n /dev/input/eventWHATEVER to get a listing of the properties udev sees it by.

  2. Construct a rule something like this which deletes it after it gets created:

KERNEL=="event[0-9]*", ATTRS{id/product}=="....", ATTRS{id/vendor}=="....", RUN+="/bin/rm -f /dev/input/%k"

Archwiki's udev page has more information on the syntax.

Q: How to identify valid bodies and convertible terms A:

Very short solution.

is_convertible_term(T) :-
    catch((! ; T), error(type_error(callable,_),_), false).

is_body(T) :-
    \+ \+ (
        term_variables(T, Vs),
        append(Vs, _, [0|Vs]),
        is_convertible_term(T)
    ).

Q: Which API's are best for E-commerce Website? A:

I would go with REST API - it is simpler and allows for faster development. Many e-commerce platforms like Shopify use REST. SOAP is reliable but is better suited for legacy systems.

Q: CS50p Question "Outdated" Check failure for one scenario A:

Just to wrap this issue up, since the comments indicate that the solution was found, the key bit was usage of the "strip()" suffix to the input statement to remove any spurious characters and/or spaces from the user entry.

x = input("Date: ").title().strip()

The key takeaway here is possible further study of Python functions and their variations such as "input" and "strip()".
